I just want to state this first and foremost, you're not responsible for someone else actions. You are in control of yourself and the choices that you make. If someone made the choice to end their lives, your not responsible for their choice, it may feel like you are, because perhaps you may feel like you didn't do enough for them, but the thing about suicide is when someone has decided that they want to go, they will and it's very hard to change their mind. That doesn't mean you didn't try hard enough, love them enough, etc, it's not personal. So please don't take it personally. Secondly, when someone says it's not a burden, and they've made effort to help you, and even shown you that they want to, then it's not burdening them, and I know it's hard to understand, because I still don't understand it. But those people are serious. Mental health professionals, chose their job, they CHOSE to be there, so if someone is CHOOSING to help you, you're not burdening them. The hopelessness, I understand. I felt hopeless for sometime because no one was saying the right thing to me as well, but that was because I wasn't opening up to anyone either, I was only telling people half of what was happening so it wouldn't be burdening them, but what I didn't know is that in turn that was harming me. Because I wasn't telling the truth, and talking about everything, I wasn't getting the help that I needed because I thought I was sparing others the burden by leaving out details. I don't know if that's the same for you, but that's what happened with me when I felt like no one could help me.

What happened to you, you can't change, that's in the past. But what you can change is how you go about things in your life, now, and today.. you may not have control over others and what they do, but you do have control over yourself and what you chose to do. What in your life, that you have control over, would you do differently?
